chunks: 1494 - The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:

No wind has ever come forth except according to a measure, except in the time of ‘Ād, for it rebelled against its keepers and came out like the eye of a needle, so it destroyed the people of ‘Ād. And no rain has ever fallen except according to a weight, except in the time of Nūḥ, peace be upon him, for it rebelled against its keepers and came out like the eye of a needle, and Allah drowned the people of Nūḥ, peace be upon him, by it.

key_terms.بِمِكْيَالٍ: by measure, indicating precise divine apportionment
key_terms.بِوَزْنٍ: by weight, indicating exact proportion and regulation
key_terms.خُزَّانِهَا: its keepers, meaning those entrusted with its restraint by Allah’s command
key_terms.رِيحٌ: wind, presented here as a created force proceeding by divine measure
key_terms.عَادٍ: the people of ‘Ād, an earlier community destroyed by punishment
key_terms.فَأَغْرَقَ: so He drowned, referring to Allah’s punishment through the flood
key_terms.مَطَرٌ: rain, described as normally descending according to measured order
key_terms.نُوحٍ: Nūḥ, peace be upon him, whose people were drowned

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Allah’s control over wind and rain in the times of ‘Ād and Nūḥ عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that natural forces such as wind and rain ordinarily proceed according to precise divine measure. It highlights the exceptional punishments sent upon the peoples of ‘Ād and Nūḥ عليه السلام, showing Allah’s absolute control over creation and the destructive consequences of divine chastisement.
